The generic nested-object schema stripped the finding fields, so the complete existing finding is preserved here as text. FINDING A-R2-01: Reclaim ownership targets when their terminals are removed. Category: correctness/performance, resource lifecycle and bounded accounting. Severity: MEDIUM; priority P2; confidence 0.98; classification MUST-FIX. Patch anchor: /Users/addomam/projects/amux-e03-build/src/control.rs:331-338 (Registry::end_target). Scenario: repeatedly open an ordinary terminal, close it, wait for exit, and remove it, including terminals with no controller, calls or claim history. Each open mints a fresh UUID at daemon.rs:565 and installs a new Target via Registry::add_target. The remove consumer at daemon.rs:1230-1274 calls end_target and removes the topology/integration records, but end_target only marks the Target ended and leaves it in Registry::targets. The only targets.remove call is inside add_target when the SAME terminal ID is replaced; runtime opens use fresh IDs, so that branch cannot reclaim these removed terminals. take_events at control.rs:802-821 prunes only Registry::retired, not Registry::targets. Consequently the registry retains every removed PTY indefinitely, even when its calls/claims are empty. Source-to-sink impact: all_targets still returns those entries; periodic tick/take_events scan them, and change_view at control.rs:1051-1076 continues inserting view facts and emitting full control-view-changed snapshots for every removed terminal. Terminal admission at daemon.rs:195-201 counts only current topology entries and in-flight opens, so normal close/remove churn bypasses any bound on this new retained state. Memory and registry work therefore grow with lifetime terminal churn rather than the configured retained-terminal limit; attachment changes additionally publish events for already removed targets and consume live event-history capacity. This is outside the narrow accepted Codex exception. Minimal fix: add an explicit registry-removal/retirement path used when a terminal is actually removed and when an unpublished open is discarded. Detach the ended Target from the live targets map, preserve only required old-call/claim history through existing Arc-bound references/retired handling, and reclaim records with no outstanding calls or claims rather than retaining them forever. Preserve ended-target rejection and late settlement for still-retained handles; do not erase unresolved work to implement reclamation. Main-agent regression to add/run after the fix: repeated real open/close/remove with empty accounting leaves live registry storage and subsequent view-event fan-out bounded, while a retained ended claim can still receive its exact late settlement. This finding is source-proven, not runtime-reproduced by this reviewer. FINDING SEC-R2-01: Concurrent close treats cleanup-started as cleanup-completed, allowing daemon exit before managed backend/resource teardown.
Severity: HIGH. Confidence: 9/10 from the source execution path; not runtime-reproduced by this reviewer. Category: owned lifecycle/privacy; improper cleanup synchronization (CWE-667). Must-fix, unwaived. This is not a cross-user authentication bypass and does not depend on treating the intentionally privileged same-user API as a sandbox.

Primary location: src/codex.rs:670-673, Instance::close. The stop.swap(true, Ordering::AcqRel) early return prevents duplicate teardown initiation but supplies no completion barrier. The winning caller still has to degrade state, shut down its socket, join its worker, terminate/reap the backend and remove the private root (src/codex.rs:675-711). Other relevant locations: src/codex.rs:600-612 (end_terminal and shutdown both call close), src/daemon.rs:617-620 (PTY exit callback calls codex.end_terminal), src/runtime.rs:377-429 (detached reaper invokes that callback), src/daemon.rs:1820-1842 (shutdown closes PTYs, waits client connections, invokes codex.shutdown and returns), src/main.rs:1-6 (return from the main thread ends the process). Private credential copies originate at src/codex.rs:345-352; backend creation uses a separate owned session at src/codex.rs:365-377. ProcessTree::terminate deliberately sleeps 200ms between TERM/CONT and its final freeze/KILL phase at src/runtime.rs:810-824.

Source-to-sink execution path: (1) A managed frontend exits, or an authorized local caller explicitly closes its terminal. The detached PTY reaper reaches the daemon exit callback and calls end_terminal -> Instance::close. (2) That thread sets stop=true before completing cleanup. It can still be joining its worker or inside backend termination's grace interval; removal of the private root has not happened. (3) A concurrent authorized shutdown reaches Broker::shutdown on the daemon main thread. Its close call sees stop=true and returns immediately rather than joining/waiting for the first cleanup owner. (4) The shutdown loop waits client connections, not PTY reaper callbacks. The hook-worker join is unrelated and does not synchronize the cleanup owner. Daemon::run and then main can therefore return while cleanup remains on the detached reaper thread. Rust process exit terminates that thread before its remaining teardown work. The backend has its own session and is not guaranteed to die with the daemon.

Realistic scenario and impact: Close a managed Codex terminal and shut down the daemon while its exit callback is cleaning up the managed instance. No forged capability, unsupported operation or payload is required. Depending on scheduling, the daemon can exit before private cx-*/codex/auth.json, copied resume history and other owned resources are removed; a backend/descendant still in termination grace can also survive until or beyond the prematurely abandoned final kill/reap phase. These are source-supported possible outcomes, not observed runtime results. The narrow upstream native-fence/optimistic-history exception explicitly does not waive private credential/resource cleanup or owned lifecycle.

Nearby controls considered: socket shutdown and worker joining correctly happen in the FIRST close caller; birth-qualified ProcessTree termination protects process identity; the ordinary cleanup path removes the private root. None makes a SECOND close caller wait for completion. Terminal::close also returns immediately after its closing flag is set, and daemon shutdown does not join the detached reaper. Existing passing cleanup evidence does not exclude this scheduling window. In tests/agent_interaction.rs:450-483, Host::drop explicitly kills fixture process groups and removes the fixture root before daemon_shutdown_reaps_fixture_children_and_removes_private_roots checks the final state (lines1913-1940); those assertions therefore do not independently establish daemon-owned completion of this race. The strengthened focus regression checks a shell-only shutdown, not concurrent managed-backend close completion.

Minimal fix: Separate stop-requested from teardown-completed. Serialize Instance::close through a dedicated cleanup ownership/completion mechanism so concurrent callers, especially Broker::shutdown, wait for the existing cleanup attempt to finish (or receive an explicit bounded incomplete-cleanup result) before shutdown returns. Keep socket shutdown able to unblock worker I/O; do not hold topology/authority locks across joins or provider I/O, and preserve birth-qualified process cleanup. Have the parent add a deterministic no-model regression that pauses the first terminal-exit cleanup after stop is set, invokes shutdown concurrently, proves shutdown cannot finish before teardown completion, then checks backend/descendant reap and private root removal BEFORE fixture fallback cleanup. No tests or edits were performed by this reviewer.
